日月金木水火土 is how a Hong Kong keyboard labels its keys A to G. Open that keyboard's picture on the site, then read the ciphertext piece by piece on the workbench.
A code is one to five letters, and seven characters use all thirty keys. Take the longest piece that reads each time, and every cut falls into place.
The last two characters name the keyboard itself. The first four say where every beginner starts.
